FOOTNOTES

1/ General Appropriations Act funds are appropriated as an Operating Lump Sum with Special Line Items by Agency.

Operating Budget

The Baseline includes \$3,693,900 and 26.4 FTE Positions from the Arizona State Board of Pharmacy Fund in FY 2027 for the operating budget. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Investigator Costs

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(60,100) from the Arizona State Board of Pharmacy Fund in FY 2027 for the elimination of one-time field investigator costs.

An FY 2026 budget footnote extends the use of \$190,500 from the board's FY 2023 appropriation until June 30, 2026, for the purpose of e-licensing system upgrades.

Prescriber Report Card

The Baseline includes \$50,000 from the Arizona State Board of Pharmacy Fund in FY 2027 for the Prescriber Report Card program. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

This line item funds the development of opioid prescriber report cards as part of the Controlled Substances Prescription Monitoring Program (CSPMP). The prescriber report cards include detailed information comparing a practitioner's history of prescribing controlled substances with peers in a similar practice.

The Baseline includes no funding from the Arizona State Board of Pharmacy Fund in FY 2027 for an Annual Leave Payout. These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

The FY 2025 appropriation of \$64,600 for the annual leave payout is non-lapsing. As of FY 2026, \$45,200 of the appropriation remains.

In September 2025, the Auditor General published a performance audit and sunset review of the Arizona State Board of Pharmacy. The audit evaluated the Board's licensing, investigations, appropriateness of fees, and availability of public information. As relates to budget implications, the Auditor General recommends the Board:

perform a comprehensive analysis to see if individual fees align with costs of providing a regulatory service.

refund permit or license fees when regulatory time frames are not met.

The Auditor General also evaluated the Board's Controlled Substances Prescription Monitoring Program (CSPMP) compliance. Statute requires prescribers of controlled substances to register with the CSPMP and utilize the database when prescribing such substances. The Auditor General found that the Board needs to improve the identification and reporting of CSPMP non-compliance to licensing boards. In addition, the report found that few licensing boards investigated or disciplined violators. As a result, the Auditor General made the following recommendations with budget implications:

Prescriber Report Card

Make statutory changes to require all Arizona prescribers to obtain a single, Board-issued controlled-substance registration and authorize the Board to enforce compliance with CSPMP requirements.

Alternatively, the report recommends that the Legislature should evaluate and revise provider licensing board statutes and processes to improve enforcement.

Identify personnel, information system changes, and methods required to assess noncompliance with CSPMP requirement.

The Board agreed with the audit findings and plans to implement or implement in a different manner all the recommendations directed to it.
